discovery.selection_rule: One earlier-in-year source before each unmatched pilot 10-K: 2014 BlackRock; 2015–2021 Vanguard. This is a bounded corroboration sample, not exhaustive ownership or identifier history

limits: These observations bind the reported issuer CIK to a reported common-stock CUSIP within each original accession. They do not identify a vendor security identifier, prove a continuous effective interval, resolve class selection, or establish historical known-at/availability.

Event dates, acceptance clocks, filing dates and date-of-filing-date-change values have distinct meanings. HTTP Last-Modified/Date and today's retrieval clock are retrieval metadata, not evidence of first public dissemination.

All eight observations are after January 1 of their own filing year. Six precede January 1, 2020; the February 2020 filing reports a December 2019 event but cannot be moved back to the January 2020 selection cutoff. The February 2021 observation is likewise retained separately.
Repeated unchanged class/CUSIP text does not prove uninterrupted CIK/security validity between observations or across control/reference/label windows.

The original eight unmatched 10-Ks remain unmatched in the frozen discovery ledger. Pairing by the already-verified original issuer and year adds context, not a new candidate, approval, exclusion, or forecasting row.
next_action: Where the authorized saved Names/CCM source exists, inspect the dated original records corresponding to this reported common-stock CUSIP as candidate corroboration, preserving competing CIKs and all original intervals. Keep vendor release/known-at evidence, historical link bounds and human class approval as separate unresolved requirements.
